C.3 Proof of Theorem 3.3

We prove a stronger pathwise statement and then pass to the terminal marginal. The derivation has two ingredients. First, the exact DPRM reveal law is a Doob hh-transform of the base reveal chain; see the classical Doob hh-transform construction and the DPRM derivation in Bu et al. (2025b). Second, the stagewise Soft-BoN approximation follows from the main KL approximation theorem of Verdun et al. (2025).

Setup. Let

τ=(S0,A0,S1,A1,…,ST−1,AT−1,ST)\tau=(S_{0},A_{0},S_{1},A_{1},\dots,S_{T-1},A_{T-1},S_{T})

be a reveal trajectory. At state s∈𝒮ts\in\mathcal{S}_{t}, the action a∈𝒜⁡(s)a\in\mathcal{A}(s) determines the next state sa∈𝒮t+1s^{a}\in\mathcal{S}_{t+1} under teacher forcing. Let R⁡(XT)∈[0,1]R(X_{T})\in[0,1] be the terminal reward. Using the base proposal q0(⋅∣s)q_{0}(\cdot\mid s) from 1, define

ℙ0​(τ)=ρ0​(S0)​∏t=0T−1q0​(At∣St),ℙβ​(τ)=exp⁡(β​R​(XT​(τ)))Zβ​ℙ0​(τ),\mathbb{P}_{0}(\tau)=\rho_{0}(S_{0})\prod_{t=0}^{T-1}q_{0}(A_{t}\mid S_{t}),\qquad\mathbb{P}_{\beta}(\tau)=\frac{\exp(\beta R(X_{T}(\tau)))}{Z_{\beta}}\,\mathbb{P}_{0}(\tau),

where

Zβ:=𝔼ℙ0​[exp⁡(β​R​(XT))].Z_{\beta}:=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{0}}\!\left[\exp(\beta R(X_{T}))\right].

Also define

ht​(s):=𝔼ℙ0​[exp⁡(β​R​(XT))∣St=s].h_{t}(s):=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{0}}\!\left[\exp(\beta R(X_{T}))\mid S_{t}=s\right].
Lemma C.18 (Backward recursion for hth_{t}).

For every non-terminal state s∈𝒮ts\in\mathcal{S}_{t},

ht​(s)=∑a∈𝒜⁡(s)q0​(a∣s)​ht+1​(sa),h_{t}(s)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal{A}(s)}q_{0}(a\mid s)\,h_{t+1}(s^{a}),

and

hT​(s)=exp⁡(β​R​(x⁡(s))),h_{T}(s)=\exp(\beta R(x(s))),

where x⁡(s)x(s) is the fully revealed response represented by ss.

Proof.

By the tower property,

ht​(s)=𝔼ℙ0​[𝔼ℙ0​[exp⁡(β​R​(XT))∣St+1]|St=s]=𝔼ℙ0​[ht+1​(St+1)∣St=s].h_{t}(s)=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{0}}\!\left[\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{0}}\!\left[\exp(\beta R(X_{T}))\mid S_{t+1}\right]\,\middle|\,S_{t}=s\right]=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{0}}\!\left[h_{t+1}(S_{t+1})\mid S_{t}=s\right].

Since St+1=saS_{t+1}=s^{a} once At=aA_{t}=a is chosen,

𝔼ℙ0​[ht+1​(St+1)∣St=s]=∑a∈𝒜⁡(s)q0​(a∣s)​ht+1​(sa).\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{0}}\!\left[h_{t+1}(S_{t+1})\mid S_{t}=s\right]=\sum_{a\in\mathcal{A}(s)}q_{0}(a\mid s)\,h_{t+1}(s^{a}).

At time TT, there is no future randomness, so

hT​(s)=𝔼ℙ0​[exp⁡(β​R​(XT))∣ST=s]=exp⁡(β​R​(x⁡(s))).h_{T}(s)=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{0}}\!\left[\exp(\beta R(X_{T}))\mid S_{T}=s\right]=\exp(\beta R(x(s))).

∎

Proposition C.19 (Exact reveal rule under the tilted path law).

For every non-terminal state s=(q,z,t)s=(q,z,t), the one-step conditional of ℙβ\mathbb{P}_{\beta} is exactly the Gibbs reveal law in 3.

Proof.

This is the standard Doob hh-transform form of the tilted path law; see the classical construction and the DPRM specialization in Bu et al. (2025b). For completeness, we verify the identity in our notation.

Fix ss and aa. By the definition of ℙβ\mathbb{P}_{\beta},

ℙβ(At=a∣St=s)∝q0(a∣s)𝔼ℙ0[exp(βR(XT))∣St=s,At=a].\mathbb{P}_{\beta}(A_{t}=a\mid S_{t}=s)\propto q_{0}(a\mid s)\,\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{0}}\!\left[\exp(\beta R(X_{T}))\mid S_{t}=s,A_{t}=a\right].

𝔼ℙ0[exp(βR(XT))∣St=s,At=a]=𝔼ℙ0[exp(βR(XT))∣St+1=sa]=ht+1(sa).\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{0}}\!\left[\exp(\beta R(X_{T}))\mid S_{t}=s,A_{t}=a\right]=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{0}}\!\left[\exp(\beta R(X_{T}))\mid S_{t+1}=s^{a}\right]=h_{t+1}(s^{a}).

ℙβ​(At=a∣St=s)∝q0​(a∣s)​ht+1​(sa).\mathbb{P}_{\beta}(A_{t}=a\mid S_{t}=s)\propto q_{0}(a\mid s)\,h_{t+1}(s^{a}).

Using Rt⋆​(a,s)=β−1​log⁡ht+1​(sa)R_{t}^{\star}(a;s)=\beta^{-1}\log h_{t+1}(s^{a}), this is exactly 3. ∎

Lemma C.20 (Bounded process reward).

If R⁡(XT)∈[0,1]R(X_{T})\in[0,1], then Rt⋆​(a,s)∈[0,1]R_{t}^{\star}(a;s)\in[0,1] for every non-terminal state ss and action a∈𝒜⁡(s)a\in\mathcal{A}(s).

At,1,…,At,N∼i.i.d.q0(⋅∣s).A_{t,1},\dots,A_{t,N}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{i.i.d.}}}{{\sim}}q_{0}(\cdot\mid s).

Proposition C.23 (Pathwise lifting of the local Soft-BoN bound).

Under the assumptions of Theorem 3.3,

𝔼⁡[KL⁡(ℙβ∥ℙ^{Nt})]≤sinh⁡(β/2)2​𝔼ℙβ​[∑t=0T−11Nt​(St)].\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathrm{KL}\!\left(\mathbb{P}_{\beta}\,\middle\|\,\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_{\{N_{t}\}}\right)\right]\leq\sinh(\beta/2)^{2}\;\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{\beta}}\!\left[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\frac{1}{N_{t}(S_{t})}\right]. (29)

In particular, if Nt​(s)≡NN_{t}(s)\equiv N, then

𝔼⁡[KL⁡(ℙβ∥ℙ^N)]≤Tsinh(β/2)2N.\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathrm{KL}\!\left(\mathbb{P}_{\beta}\,\middle\|\,\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_{N}\right)\right]\leq\frac{T\,\sinh(\beta/2)^{2}}{N}. (30)
Proof.

Condition on the shortlist randomness. By Lem. C.22,

KL(ℙβ∥ℙ^{Nt})=𝔼ℙβ[∑t=0T−1KL(πt⋆(⋅∣St)∥π^t,Nt​(St)(⋅∣St))].\mathrm{KL}\!\left(\mathbb{P}_{\beta}\,\middle\|\,\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_{\{N_{t}\}}\right)=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{\beta}}\!\left[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathrm{KL}\!\left(\pi_{t}^{\star}(\cdot\mid S_{t})\,\middle\|\,\widehat{\pi}_{t,N_{t}(S_{t})}(\cdot\mid S_{t})\right)\right].

Now take expectation over the shortlist randomness. Since the sum is finite, Tonelli’s theorem gives

𝔼[KL(ℙβ∥ℙ^{Nt})]=𝔼ℙβ[∑t=0T−1𝔼[KL(πt⋆(⋅∣St)∥π^t,Nt​(St)(⋅∣St))|St]].\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathrm{KL}\!\left(\mathbb{P}_{\beta}\,\middle\|\,\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_{\{N_{t}\}}\right)\right]=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_{\beta}}\!\left[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathrm{KL}\!\left(\pi_{t}^{\star}(\cdot\mid S_{t})\,\middle\|\,\widehat{\pi}_{t,N_{t}(S_{t})}(\cdot\mid S_{t})\right)\,\middle|\,S_{t}\right]\right].

For each realized state St=sS_{t}=s, Prop. C.21 yields

𝔼[KL(πt⋆(⋅∣s)∥π^t,Nt​(s)(⋅∣s))]≤sinh⁡(β/2)2Nt​(s).\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathrm{KL}\!\left(\pi_{t}^{\star}(\cdot\mid s)\,\middle\|\,\widehat{\pi}_{t,N_{t}(s)}(\cdot\mid s)\right)\right]\leq\frac{\sinh(\beta/2)^{2}}{N_{t}(s)}.

Substituting this bound gives 29. If Nt​(s)≡NN_{t}(s)\equiv N, then

∑t=0T−11Nt​(St)=TN,\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\frac{1}{N_{t}(S_{t})}=\frac{T}{N},

so 30 follows. ∎

Proof of Theorem 3.3.

By Prop. C.23,

𝔼⁡[KL⁡(ℙβ∥ℙ^N)]≤Tsinh(β/2)2N.\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathrm{KL}\!\left(\mathbb{P}_{\beta}\,\middle\|\,\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_{N}\right)\right]\leq\frac{T\,\sinh(\beta/2)^{2}}{N}.

The terminal output is a measurable function of the full reveal trajectory. Hence the data-processing inequality for KL divergence gives

𝔼⁡[KL⁡(νβ∥ν^N)]≤𝔼⁡[KL⁡(ℙβ∥ℙ^N)]≤Tsinh(β/2)2N,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathrm{KL}\!\left(\nu_{\beta}\,\middle\|\,\widehat{\nu}_{N}\right)\right]\leq\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathrm{KL}\!\left(\mathbb{P}_{\beta}\,\middle\|\,\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_{N}\right)\right]\leq\frac{T\,\sinh(\beta/2)^{2}}{N},

which is exactly 12. ∎

C.4 Finite-sample forward-KL separations for Progressive Online DPRM

This appendix studies a finite-sample question left open by Proposition 3.1. Admissible token orders do not change the population minimizer, so the relevant issue is not asymptotic consistency but optimization complexity: which aligned order family drives the training KL below a target level ε\varepsilon fastest?

We analyze this question in two stages. In the early stage, we show that if confidence is a good proxy for local gradient scale, then confidence-driven progressive training is exponentially faster than random aligned-order sampling. This view mirrors curriculum learning Bu et al. (2025a) and active learning Bu et al. (2024). In the late stage, we show that if confidence-only training undersamples a residual order family that is still necessary for final KL convergence, then a sufficiently accurate DPRM guidance yields an exponential speedup over confidence-only training.

The analysis uses three standard ingredients. First, in unbiased importance-weighted SGD, the conditional second moment is minimized by sampling in proportion to gradient norm (Zhao and Zhang, 2015; El Hanchi et al., 2022). Second, arbitrary-sampling SGD admits convergence recursions controlled by that second moment (Gower et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2023). Third, confidence gating imposes a hard entropy cap and thus a support-narrowing effect (Fang et al., 2026, Proposition 2).

Stagewise forward-KL objective.

Fix a training stage tt. For each sample xx, let 𝒪t​(x)\mathcal{O}_{t}(x) be an aligned local order family. This may consist of reveal actions, reveal prefixes, or any other local order objects that can be visited both by teacher-forced training and by the corresponding inference-time controller at stage tt. Let ut(⋅∣x)u_{t}(\cdot\mid x) be a reference aligned sampling law on 𝒪t​(x)\mathcal{O}_{t}(x).

Let pt⋆(⋅∣x,o)p_{t}^{\star}(\cdot\mid x,o) be the target conditional at stage tt and let pθ(⋅∣x,o)p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x,o) be the model conditional. Define the stagewise forward-KL objective

𝒦t(θ):=𝔼x∼P^n𝔼o∼ut(⋅∣x)[KL(pt⋆(⋅∣x,o)∥pθ(⋅∣x,o))].\mathcal{K}_{t}(\theta):=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\widehat{P}_{n}}\mathbb{E}_{o\sim u_{t}(\cdot\mid x)}\Big[\mathrm{KL}\bigl(p_{t}^{\star}(\cdot\mid x,o)\,\|\,p_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x,o)\bigr)\Big]. (31)

Equivalently, 𝒦t​(θ)\mathcal{K}_{t}(\theta) is the excess stagewise cross-entropy up to an additive constant independent of θ\theta.

Let ℓt​(θ,x,o,ξ)\ell_{t}(\theta;x,o,\xi) be a stochastic per-order loss whose conditional expectation equals the integrand of 31, and define

gt​(θ,x,o,ξ):=∇θℓt​(θ,x,o,ξ),νt​(θ,x,o):=(𝔼ξ​‖gt​(θ,x,o,ξ)‖22)1/2.g_{t}(\theta;x,o,\xi):=\nabla_{\theta}\ell_{t}(\theta;x,o,\xi),\qquad\nu_{t}(\theta;x,o):=\Big(\mathbb{E}_{\xi}\|g_{t}(\theta;x,o,\xi)\|_{2}^{2}\Big)^{1/2}.

If Ot∼pt(⋅∣Xt)O_{t}\sim p_{t}(\cdot\mid X_{t}), the unbiased importance-weighted gradient estimator is

G^t(p):=ut​(Ot∣Xt)pt​(Ot∣Xt)​gt​(θt,Xt,Ot,ξt),\widehat{G}_{t}^{(p)}:=\frac{u_{t}(O_{t}\mid X_{t})}{p_{t}(O_{t}\mid X_{t})}\,g_{t}(\theta_{t};X_{t},O_{t},\xi_{t}), (32)

with conditional second moment

ℳt​(p):=𝔼⁡[‖G^t(p)‖22∣θt].\mathcal{M}_{t}(p):=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|\widehat{G}_{t}^{(p)}\|_{2}^{2}\mid\theta_{t}\right]. (33)
Assumption C.24 (Stagewise smoothness and PL geometry).

At stage tt, the forward-KL objective 𝒦t\mathcal{K}_{t} is LtL_{t}-smooth and satisfies the Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality with constant μt>0\mu_{t}>0:

12​‖∇𝒦t​(θ)‖22≥μt​(𝒦t​(θ)−𝒦t⋆)for all relevant ​θ.\frac{1}{2}\|\nabla\mathcal{K}_{t}(\theta)\|_{2}^{2}\geq\mu_{t}\bigl(\mathcal{K}_{t}(\theta)-\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\star}\bigr)\qquad\text{for all relevant }\theta.
Assumption C.25 (Confidence as a proxy for local gradient scale).

There exists a confidence-induced order score ct​(x,o)≥0c_{t}(x,o)\geq 0 and a constant κt≥1\kappa_{t}\geq 1 such that

κt−1​νt​(θt,x,o)≤ct​(x,o)≤κt​νt​(θt,x,o)for all ​x,o.\kappa_{t}^{-1}\nu_{t}(\theta_{t};x,o)\leq c_{t}(x,o)\leq\kappa_{t}\nu_{t}(\theta_{t};x,o)\qquad\text{for all }x,o.
Early stage: confidence beats random.
Assumption C.26 (Early importance concentration).

For each sample xx, there exists a subset ℰt​(x)⊆𝒪t​(x)\mathcal{E}_{t}(x)\subseteq\mathcal{O}_{t}(x) such that:

  1. 1.

    Most gradient mass lies on ℰt​(x)\mathcal{E}_{t}(x):

    ∑o∈ℰt​(x)ut​(o∣x)​νt​(θt,x,o)≥(1−ρt)​∑o∈𝒪t​(x)ut​(o∣x)​νt​(θt,x,o)\sum_{o\in\mathcal{E}_{t}(x)}u_{t}(o\mid x)\,\nu_{t}(\theta_{t};x,o)\geq(1-\rho_{t})\sum_{o\in\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)}u_{t}(o\mid x)\,\nu_{t}(\theta_{t};x,o)

    for some ρt∈[0,1)\rho_{t}\in[0,1);

  2. 2.

    The easy family is exponentially smaller than the full aligned family:

    |𝒪t​(x)||ℰt​(x)|≥eat​dt\frac{|\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)|}{|\mathcal{E}_{t}(x)|}\geq e^{a_{t}d_{t}}

    for some stage-difficulty parameter dt≥1d_{t}\geq 1 and constant at>0a_{t}>0.

Lemma C.27 (Variance-optimal proposal over aligned order families).

For fixed θt\theta_{t}, the proposal minimizing ℳt​(p)\mathcal{M}_{t}(p) satisfies

ptopt​(o∣x)∝ut​(o∣x)​νt​(θt,x,o).p_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}(o\mid x)\propto u_{t}(o\mid x)\,\nu_{t}(\theta_{t};x,o). (34)
Proof.

Condition on xx. By 32 and 33,

ℳt​(p∣x)=∑o∈𝒪t​(x)ut​(o∣x)2pt​(o∣x)​νt​(θt,x,o)2.\mathcal{M}_{t}(p\mid x)=\sum_{o\in\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)}\frac{u_{t}(o\mid x)^{2}}{p_{t}(o\mid x)}\,\nu_{t}(\theta_{t};x,o)^{2}.

Hence, for each fixed xx, the problem is

minp(⋅∣x)∈Δ(𝒪t(x))∑o∈𝒪t​(x)ut​(o∣x)2​νt​(θt,x,o)2p⁡(o∣x).\min_{p(\cdot\mid x)\in\Delta(\mathcal{O}_{t}(x))}\sum_{o\in\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)}\frac{u_{t}(o\mid x)^{2}\nu_{t}(\theta_{t};x,o)^{2}}{p(o\mid x)}.

This is exactly the conditional-variance minimization problem of importance-sampling SGD (Zhao and Zhang, 2015; El Hanchi et al., 2022). By Cauchy–Schwarz or a Lagrange multiplier, the minimizer is

ptopt​(o∣x)=ut​(o∣x)​νt​(θt,x,o)∑o′ut​(o′∣x)​νt​(θt,x,o′).p_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}(o\mid x)=\frac{u_{t}(o\mid x)\nu_{t}(\theta_{t};x,o)}{\sum_{o^{\prime}}u_{t}(o^{\prime}\mid x)\nu_{t}(\theta_{t};x,o^{\prime})}.

∎

Define the confidence proposal

ptconf​(o∣x):=ut​(o∣x)​ct​(x,o)∑o′ut​(o′∣x)​ct​(x,o′),p_{t}^{\mathrm{conf}}(o\mid x):=\frac{u_{t}(o\mid x)c_{t}(x,o)}{\sum_{o^{\prime}}u_{t}(o^{\prime}\mid x)c_{t}(x,o^{\prime})}, (35)

and the random aligned proposal

ptrand​(o∣x):=1|𝒪t​(x)|.p_{t}^{\mathrm{rand}}(o\mid x):=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)|}. (36)
Lemma C.28 (Second-moment comparison).

Under Assumptions C.25 and C.26,

ℳt​(ptconf)≤κt2​ℳt​(ptopt),\mathcal{M}_{t}\!\bigl(p_{t}^{\mathrm{conf}}\bigr)\leq\kappa_{t}^{2}\,\mathcal{M}_{t}\!\bigl(p_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}\bigr), (37)

and

ℳt​(ptrand)≥(1−ρt)2​eat​dt​ℳt​(ptopt).\mathcal{M}_{t}\!\bigl(p_{t}^{\mathrm{rand}}\bigr)\geq(1-\rho_{t})^{2}e^{a_{t}d_{t}}\,\mathcal{M}_{t}\!\bigl(p_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}\bigr). (38)
Proof.

The first bound follows from Assumption C.25: the proposal ptconfp_{t}^{\mathrm{conf}} is a κt2\kappa_{t}^{2}-multiplicative approximation to ptoptp_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}, so substituting into 33 yields 37.

For the second bound, condition on xx and write

ao:=ut​(o∣x)​νt​(θt,x,o).a_{o}:=u_{t}(o\mid x)\nu_{t}(\theta_{t};x,o).

Then

ℳt​(ptrand∣x)=|𝒪t​(x)|∑o∈𝒪t​(x)ao2≥|𝒪t​(x)|​∑o∈ℰt​(x)ao2.\mathcal{M}_{t}(p_{t}^{\mathrm{rand}}\mid x)=|\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)|\sum_{o\in\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)}a_{o}^{2}\geq|\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)|\sum_{o\in\mathcal{E}_{t}(x)}a_{o}^{2}.

By Cauchy–Schwarz,

∑o∈ℰt​(x)ao2≥1|ℰt​(x)|​(∑o∈ℰt​(x)ao)2.\sum_{o\in\mathcal{E}_{t}(x)}a_{o}^{2}\geq\frac{1}{|\mathcal{E}_{t}(x)|}\left(\sum_{o\in\mathcal{E}_{t}(x)}a_{o}\right)^{2}.

Using Assumption C.26,

∑o∈ℰt​(x)ao≥(1−ρt)​∑o∈𝒪t​(x)ao.\sum_{o\in\mathcal{E}_{t}(x)}a_{o}\geq(1-\rho_{t})\sum_{o\in\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)}a_{o}.

Therefore

ℳt​(ptrand∣x)≥|𝒪t​(x)||ℰt​(x)|​(1−ρt)2​(∑o∈𝒪t​(x)ao)2.\mathcal{M}_{t}(p_{t}^{\mathrm{rand}}\mid x)\geq\frac{|\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)|}{|\mathcal{E}_{t}(x)|}(1-\rho_{t})^{2}\left(\sum_{o\in\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)}a_{o}\right)^{2}.

But

(∑o∈𝒪t​(x)ao)2=ℳt​(ptopt∣x),\left(\sum_{o\in\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)}a_{o}\right)^{2}=\mathcal{M}_{t}(p_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}}\mid x),

and |𝒪t​(x)|/|ℰt​(x)|≥eat​dt|\mathcal{O}_{t}(x)|/|\mathcal{E}_{t}(x)|\geq e^{a_{t}d_{t}}. Averaging over xx proves 38. ∎

Define the ε\varepsilon-sample complexity at stage tt by

Tt(p)​(ε):=min⁡{N:𝔼⁡[𝒦t​(θN)−𝒦t⋆]≤ε}.T_{t}^{(p)}(\varepsilon):=\min\Bigl\{N:\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{K}_{t}(\theta_{N})-\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\star}]\leq\varepsilon\Bigr\}.
Theorem C.29 (Early-stage exponential separation: confidence vs random).

Suppose Assumptions C.24, C.25, and C.26 hold. Consider constant-step unbiased SGD using the estimator 32.

Then there exists a stepsize choice for confidence-driven aligned training such that

Tt(conf)​(ε)=O⁡(Lt​κt2​ℳt​(ptopt)μt2​ε​log⁡𝒦t​(θ0)−𝒦t⋆ε).T_{t}^{(\mathrm{conf})}(\varepsilon)=O\!\left(\frac{L_{t}\kappa_{t}^{2}\,\mathcal{M}_{t}(p_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}})}{\mu_{t}^{2}\,\varepsilon}\log\frac{\mathcal{K}_{t}(\theta_{0})-\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\star}}{\varepsilon}\right). (39)

Moreover, any constant-stepsize random aligned-order SGD whose asymptotic error floor is at most ε/2\varepsilon/2 must satisfy

Tt(rand)​(ε)=Ω⁡(Lt​(1−ρt)2​eat​dt​ℳt​(ptopt)μt2​ε​log⁡𝒦t​(θ0)−𝒦t⋆ε).T_{t}^{(\mathrm{rand})}(\varepsilon)=\Omega\!\left(\frac{L_{t}(1-\rho_{t})^{2}e^{a_{t}d_{t}}\,\mathcal{M}_{t}(p_{t}^{\mathrm{opt}})}{\mu_{t}^{2}\,\varepsilon}\log\frac{\mathcal{K}_{t}(\theta_{0})-\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\star}}{\varepsilon}\right). (40)

Hence confidence-driven progressive training enjoys an exponential sample-complexity improvement over random aligned-order training, up to the calibration factor κt2\kappa_{t}^{2}.

Proof.

For any proposal pp, smoothness and unbiasedness give the standard recursion

𝔼⁡[𝒦t​(θk+1)−𝒦t⋆∣θk]≤(1−μt​ηt)​(𝒦t​(θk)−𝒦t⋆)+Lt​ηt22​ℳt​(p),\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{K}_{t}(\theta_{k+1})-\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\star}\mid\theta_{k}]\leq(1-\mu_{t}\eta_{t})\bigl(\mathcal{K}_{t}(\theta_{k})-\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\star}\bigr)+\frac{L_{t}\eta_{t}^{2}}{2}\mathcal{M}_{t}(p),

as in the arbitrary-sampling SGD literature (Gower et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2023).

For the confidence proposal, choose

ηt=Θ⁡(μt​εLt​ℳt​(ptconf)).\eta_{t}=\Theta\!\left(\frac{\mu_{t}\varepsilon}{L_{t}\mathcal{M}_{t}(p_{t}^{\mathrm{conf}})}\right).

Then the additive noise floor is O⁡(ε)O(\varepsilon), and unrolling the recursion yields

Tt(conf)​(ε)=O⁡(Lt​ℳt​(ptconf)μt2​ε​log⁡𝒦t​(θ0)−𝒦t⋆ε).T_{t}^{(\mathrm{conf})}(\varepsilon)=O\!\left(\frac{L_{t}\mathcal{M}_{t}(p_{t}^{\mathrm{conf}})}{\mu_{t}^{2}\,\varepsilon}\log\frac{\mathcal{K}_{t}(\theta_{0})-\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\star}}{\varepsilon}\right).

Using 37 gives 39.

For the random proposal, any constant stepsize with asymptotic floor at most ε/2\varepsilon/2 must satisfy

Lt​ηt2​μt​ℳt​(ptrand)≤ε2,\frac{L_{t}\eta_{t}}{2\mu_{t}}\mathcal{M}_{t}(p_{t}^{\mathrm{rand}})\leq\frac{\varepsilon}{2},

hence

ηt≤μt​εLt​ℳt​(ptrand).\eta_{t}\leq\frac{\mu_{t}\varepsilon}{L_{t}\mathcal{M}_{t}(p_{t}^{\mathrm{rand}})}.

Therefore the contraction factor cannot exceed 1−μt​ηt1-\mu_{t}\eta_{t}, so to shrink the initial KL down to ε\varepsilon requires at least

Ω⁡(Lt​ℳt​(ptrand)μt2​ε​log⁡𝒦t​(θ0)−𝒦t⋆ε)\Omega\!\left(\frac{L_{t}\mathcal{M}_{t}(p_{t}^{\mathrm{rand}})}{\mu_{t}^{2}\,\varepsilon}\log\frac{\mathcal{K}_{t}(\theta_{0})-\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\star}}{\varepsilon}\right)

iterations. Using 38 yields 40. ∎

Late stage: DPRM beats confidence-only.

We now analyze the stage after warmup. Here the issue is no longer variance-optimality, but undercoverage. We assume that there remains a residual family of orders that is necessary for final KL convergence, but confidence-only training visits it too rarely.

We first restate the entropy-cap result of Fang et al. (2026, Proposition 2).

Proposition C.30 (Entropy cap under confidence gating (Fang et al., 2026, Prop. 2)).

Assume the decoder is (1−δ)(1-\delta)-gated. Then the induced sequence distribution XX satisfies

H⁡(X)≤L​hV​(δ),Beff:=exp⁡(H⁡(X)/L)≤exp⁡(hV​(δ)),H(X)\leq Lh_{V}(\delta),\qquad B_{\mathrm{eff}}:=\exp(H(X)/L)\leq\exp(h_{V}(\delta)), (41)

where hV​(δ)=hb​(δ)+δ​log⁡(|V|−1)h_{V}(\delta)=h_{b}(\delta)+\delta\log(|V|-1).

Assumption C.31 (Late-stage residual family and confidence undercoverage).

For each late-stage state ss, let 𝒪t​(s)\mathcal{O}_{t}(s) be the reachable local order family and let ℛt​(s)⊆𝒪t​(s)\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)\subseteq\mathcal{O}_{t}(s) be a residual family with the following properties.

  1. 1.

    Residual score gap. The exact DPRM score gap

    Δtres​(s):=info∈ℛt​(s)gt⋆​(o,s)−supo∈𝒪t​(s)∖ℛt​(s)gt⋆​(o,s)\Delta_{t}^{\mathrm{res}}(s):=\inf_{o\in\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)}g_{t}^{\star}(o;s)-\sup_{o\in\mathcal{O}_{t}(s)\setminus\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)}g_{t}^{\star}(o;s)

    is strictly positive.

  2. 2.

    Confidence undercoverage. Under confidence-only training,

    πtconf​(ℛt​(s)∣s)≤Ct​e−bt​ht\pi_{t}^{\mathrm{conf}}(\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)\mid s)\leq C_{t}e^{-b_{t}h_{t}}

    for some structural difficulty parameter ht≥1h_{t}\geq 1, constant bt>0b_{t}>0, and Ct≥1C_{t}\geq 1.

  3. 3.

    Residual KL contraction. Let 𝒦tres​(θ)\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\mathrm{res}}(\theta) denote the contribution of ℛt\mathcal{R}_{t} to the stagewise forward KL. There exists γt∈(0,1]\gamma_{t}\in(0,1] such that, conditional on sampling an order from ℛt​(s)\mathcal{R}_{t}(s),

    𝔼[𝒦t+1res(θ)∣θt,Ot∈ℛt(s)]≤(1−γt)𝒦tres(θt),\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{K}_{t+1}^{\mathrm{res}}(\theta)\mid\theta_{t},\,O_{t}\in\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)]\leq(1-\gamma_{t})\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\mathrm{res}}(\theta_{t}),

    whereas conditional on sampling outside ℛt​(s)\mathcal{R}_{t}(s),

    𝔼[𝒦t+1res(θ)∣θt,Ot∉ℛt(s)]≤𝒦tres(θt).\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{K}_{t+1}^{\mathrm{res}}(\theta)\mid\theta_{t},\,O_{t}\notin\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)]\leq\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\mathrm{res}}(\theta_{t}).
Theorem C.32 (Late-stage exponential separation: DPRM vs confidence-only).

Assume Assumption C.31. Let

ϵt​(s):=supo∈𝒪t​(s)|g^t​(o,s)−gt⋆​(o,s)|\epsilon_{t}(s):=\sup_{o\in\mathcal{O}_{t}(s)}|\widehat{g}_{t}(o;s)-g_{t}^{\star}(o;s)|

be the total stage-2 score error, including online estimation and any shortlist approximation error. Suppose that after warmup,

ϵt​(s)<Δtres​(s)2for all relevant ​s.\epsilon_{t}(s)<\frac{\Delta_{t}^{\mathrm{res}}(s)}{2}\qquad\text{for all relevant }s.

Then:

  1. 1.

    the practical stage-2 proposal over 𝒪t​(s)\mathcal{O}_{t}(s) assigns residual-family mass at least

    π^t​(ℛt​(s)∣s)≥|ℛt​(s)|​eΔtres​(s)−2​ϵt​(s)|ℛt​(s)|​eΔtres​(s)−2​ϵt​(s)+|𝒪t​(s)∖ℛt​(s)|;\widehat{\pi}_{t}(\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)\mid s)\geq\frac{|\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)|\,e^{\Delta_{t}^{\mathrm{res}}(s)-2\epsilon_{t}(s)}}{|\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)|\,e^{\Delta_{t}^{\mathrm{res}}(s)-2\epsilon_{t}(s)}+|\mathcal{O}_{t}(s)\setminus\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)|}; (42)
  2. 2.

    if, in addition,

    Δtres​(s)−2​ϵt​(s)≥bt​ht+log⁡|𝒪t​(s)∖ℛt​(s)||ℛt​(s)|+ct\Delta_{t}^{\mathrm{res}}(s)-2\epsilon_{t}(s)\geq b_{t}h_{t}+\log\frac{|\mathcal{O}_{t}(s)\setminus\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)|}{|\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)|}+c_{t}

    for some ct>0c_{t}>0, then

    π^t​(ℛt​(s)∣s)≥11+e−ct=:ptDPRM,\widehat{\pi}_{t}(\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)\mid s)\geq\frac{1}{1+e^{-c_{t}}}=:p_{t}^{\mathrm{DPRM}}, (43)

    whereas

    πtconf​(ℛt​(s)∣s)≤Ct​e−bt​ht.\pi_{t}^{\mathrm{conf}}(\mathcal{R}_{t}(s)\mid s)\leq C_{t}e^{-b_{t}h_{t}}.

Consequently, if

Tt,late(conf)​(ε)andTt,late(DPRM)​(ε)T_{t,\mathrm{late}}^{(\mathrm{conf})}(\varepsilon)\quad\text{and}\quad T_{t,\mathrm{late}}^{(\mathrm{DPRM})}(\varepsilon)

denote the numbers of late-stage updates needed to drive the residual forward KL below ε\varepsilon, then

Tt,late(conf)​(ε)=Ω⁡(ebt​htγt​Ct​log⁡𝒦tres​(θTwarm)ε),T_{t,\mathrm{late}}^{(\mathrm{conf})}(\varepsilon)=\Omega\!\left(\frac{e^{b_{t}h_{t}}}{\gamma_{t}C_{t}}\log\frac{\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\mathrm{res}}(\theta_{T_{\mathrm{warm}}})}{\varepsilon}\right), (44)

whereas

Tt,late(DPRM)​(ε)=O⁡(1γt​ptDPRM​log⁡𝒦tres​(θTwarm)ε).T_{t,\mathrm{late}}^{(\mathrm{DPRM})}(\varepsilon)=O\!\left(\frac{1}{\gamma_{t}p_{t}^{\mathrm{DPRM}}}\log\frac{\mathcal{K}_{t}^{\mathrm{res}}(\theta_{T_{\mathrm{warm}}})}{\varepsilon}\right). (45)

Thus, under the stated score-gap condition, stage-2 DPRM enjoys an exponential sample-complexity improvement over confidence-only training in the late stage.

Proof.

g^t​(o,s)−g^t​(o′,s)≥gt⋆​(o,s)−gt⋆​(o′,s)−2​ϵt​(s)≥Δtres​(s)−2​ϵt​(s).\widehat{g}_{t}(o;s)-\widehat{g}_{t}(o^{\prime};s)\geq g_{t}^{\star}(o;s)-g_{t}^{\star}(o^{\prime};s)-2\epsilon_{t}(s)\geq\Delta_{t}^{\mathrm{res}}(s)-2\epsilon_{t}(s).

11+e−ct,\frac{1}{1+e^{-c_{t}}},

which proves 43.

For the residual forward KL, let pp be the probability that the current proposal samples from ℛt​(s)\mathcal{R}_{t}(s). By Assumption C.31(3),

𝔼⁡[𝒦k+1res∣θk]≤(1−γt​p)​𝒦kres.\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{K}_{k+1}^{\mathrm{res}}\mid\theta_{k}]\leq(1-\gamma_{t}p)\,\mathcal{K}_{k}^{\mathrm{res}}.

Iterating gives

𝔼⁡[𝒦kres]≤(1−γt​p)k​𝒦0res≤e−γt​p​k​𝒦0res.\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{K}_{k}^{\mathrm{res}}]\leq(1-\gamma_{t}p)^{k}\,\mathcal{K}_{0}^{\mathrm{res}}\leq e^{-\gamma_{t}pk}\,\mathcal{K}_{0}^{\mathrm{res}}.

Hence reaching ε\varepsilon requires

k≥1γt​p​log⁡𝒦0resε.k\geq\frac{1}{\gamma_{t}p}\log\frac{\mathcal{K}_{0}^{\mathrm{res}}}{\varepsilon}.

Under confidence-only training, p≤Ct​e−bt​htp\leq C_{t}e^{-b_{t}h_{t}}, which yields 44. Under DPRM, p≥ptDPRMp\geq p_{t}^{\mathrm{DPRM}}, which yields 45. ∎

Corollary C.33 (Practical stage-2 separation under online tracking).

Assume the conditions of Theorem C.32. Suppose further that the online score-tracking theorem gives

ϵt​(s)=O⁡(β​ηt​(s)​log⁡(𝒩/δ)Nmin,t​(s)+β​ηt​(s)​log⁡(𝒩/δ)Nmin,t​(s)+Biast⁡(s;δ))\epsilon_{t}(s)=O\!\left(\beta\eta_{t}(s)\sqrt{\frac{\log(\mathcal{N}/\delta)}{N_{\min,t}(s)}}+\beta\eta_{t}(s)\frac{\log(\mathcal{N}/\delta)}{N_{\min,t}(s)}+\operatorname{Bias}_{t}(s;\delta)\right)

with probability at least 1−δ1-\delta, as in Theorem 3.2. If TwarmT_{\mathrm{warm}} is chosen so that this bound is smaller than Δtres​(s)/2\Delta_{t}^{\mathrm{res}}(s)/2 for all relevant late-stage states, then the exponential late-stage separation 44 and 45 holds for the practical Progressive Online DPRM controller.

Proof.

Immediate from Theorem 3.2 and Theorem C.32. ∎

Remark C.34.

The results above separate the roles of the two stages. The early confidence stage is justified by optimization-noise reduction and can be exponentially faster than random aligned-order training under the importance-concentration assumption. The late DPRM stage is justified by residual-family rescue and can be exponentially faster than confidence-only training once the online score is accurate enough and the residual family remains necessary for final KL convergence. Together, these results provide a finite-sample explanation for why Progressive Online DPRM can help even though admissible orders do not change the population minimizer.
